headline: Warned planBTV New North End changes for public hearing and referred Natural Resource Overlay amendment ZA-27-03 to hearing
summary: The commission reviewed planBTV New North End, including soft-site analysis and the Bend Ethan Allen Design Vision, and voted to warn the amended plan for a public hearing on October 6th. It also discussed the Tier 1A update on Act 250 and Act 181, and reviewed proposed CDO Amendment ZA-27-03 on Natural Resource Overlay updates, which was referred for a public hearing on October 6th. The commission also adopted its minutes.
decisions: Approved, as amended, warning the planBTV New North End changes for a public hearing on October 6th at 7pm, with the cemetery parcel re-scored to 1.
Referred proposed CDO Amendment ZA-27-03 Natural Resource Overlay Updates to a public hearing on October 6th, with one abstention.
Adopted the minutes, with a note that the August 11th IZ meeting, Proposal 3, needs to be adjusted.

decision_evidence.quote: *Amended* Changes Warned for Public Hearing as presented on October 6th at 7pm ... Vote: Passes, Unanimous
Motion: Proposed Amendment go to Public Hearing 20:39:00 ... Vote: Passes, one abstention by M.Gaughan ... Referred for public hearing on October 6th
Action: Adopt Minutes ... Vote: Passes ... Notes or Corrections: August 11th IZ meeting, Proposal 3, note to be adjusted

Burlington Planning Commission 
Tuesday, September 15th, 2026, 6:30 P.M. 
Hybrid Meeting via Zoom and in City Hall’s Bushor Conference Room 
Draft Minutes 
 
Commissioners Present: City Staff Present: 
☒ Andy Montroll 
☐ Ryan Nick 
☒ Alexander Friend 
☒ Michael Gaughan 
Virtual  
☒ Erhard Mahnke 
☒ Erin Malone 
☒ Julia Randall 
 
 
☒ Charles Dillard, Director, Office of 
City Planning 
☒ Sarah Morgan, Principal Planner 
☒ Scott Gustin, Division Manager, P&I 
Public Attendance: Alice Rudd, Sharon Bushor, Audrey Whalen, Melo Grant 
 
 
1. Agenda  
Call to Order: 18:34:00 
Changes to Agenda:  
 
• Added item 6, update on the City’s Tier 1A application. 
 
2. Public Forum 
 
• A. Rudd: Expressed strong opposition to planBTV NNE, highlighting the soft site analysis that 
reviewed all parcels for potential development, including a Jewish cemetery. Called for the plan 
to be sent back for a full year for additional community engagement.  
• S. Bushor, asked, “Is the currently defined open space is protected or not?” She went on to ask 
questions about the North Ave. Alliance Church and the Ethan Allen Shopping Center. Expressed 
concerns over shared use paths. Went on to share thoughts about Tier 1A amendment and 
application. 
• A. Whalen, expressed concerns about Act250 exemption and the potential for lack of 
environmental review.  
• Councilor Grant raised concerns related to fences, asking for a status update on the past 
amendment. 
o C. Dillard responded letting Councilor Grant know that the City Council Ordinance 
Committee deferred action for the time being but that he would circle back. 
 
3. Chair’s Report 18:53:00 
 
• No Report Given.
Burlington Planning Commission Minutes   
 
 
 
4. Director’s Report 18:53:00 
 
• Initially no report to be given but C.Dillard responded to a question by E.Malone regarding 
Vegetation Ordinance.  
 
5. Updated 2026 Meeting Schedule 18:56:00 
 
• S.Morgan shared a slide outlining the updated 2026 meeting schedule.  
 
6. Review of planBTV New North End 18:57:00 
 
• S.Morgan presented. Gave summary of the 9/10 Community Meeting. Two primary provisions 
following that meeting; one related to soft-site analysis and the other being Bend Ethan Allen 
Design Vision.  
 
• Changes Warned for Public Hearing as presented on October 6th at 7pm 
Motioned by: E.Mahnke  
Seconded by: E.Malone 
 
• E.Mahnke asked about the significance of the Soft Site score in regards to the inclusion of an 
existing cemetery. C.Dillard responded. S.Morgan also commented on the City’s limited GIS data 
and lack of privately owned cemetery data. 
• E.Mahnke suggests an amendment to the plan and requested that the cemetery parcel be re-
scored to 1. 
 
• *Amended* Changes Warned for Public Hearing as presented on October 6th at 7pm 
Motioned by: E.Mahnke  
Seconded by: E.Malone 
Vote: Passes, Unanimous 
 
7. Tier 1A Update 
• C.Dillard gave some background information on Act 47. This is the legislation that created the 
statewide housing target. Act 181 serves as the mechanism that facilitating hitting those housing 
targets. Goes on to cover Act 250 exemptions, Act 181 design structure a nd the Tier 1A Proposal.  
• E.Mahnke voiced concerns over staff capacity as it was a topic that had been flagged in the 
previous meeting in terms of increasing development expect from Act 250. S.Gustin responded 
to these concerns. Stated that it is unclear how much staff capacity will be affected as most Act 
250 permits lack geo-referencing. Workload will become clearer in time..  
• M.Gaughan asked what the appeal/approval process would look like. Determined that it would 
be based on current ordinance. Continued to express concerns about potential for inadvertently 
restricting themselves when adopting this language from the state.  
• E.Mahnke asked if the responsibility of identifying and geolocating these projects should not fall 
on the City. Expresses concerns about the map readability. 
• S.Morgan shares document with the commission to illustrate the CDO and Act250. 
 
8. Proposed CDO Amendment ZA-27-03 Natural Resource Overlay Updates 19:49:00
Burlington Planning Commission Minutes   
 
 
 
• Three parts to this amendment 
o Article 4, Natural Resource Overlay District: Wetlands 
o Article 4, Natural Resource Overlay District: Significant Natural Communities and Rare , 
Threatened, and Endangered Species  
o Article 13, Specimen Trees  
• S.Gustin shared state and local overlay wetland maps. M.Gaughan comments on the layers and 
discrepancies or lack thereof.  
• E.Mahnke asked S.Gustin if in his professional opinion, the city significantly adding to the current 
wetland areas. S.Gustin responded, No. Any additional wetland areas identified by the state to be 
added are very small.  
• S.Morgan moved on to the second item, Natural Communities etc. This amendment serves as a 
solution to bridge the gap to get to Tier 1A. Establishes review process for properties that are 10 
acres or more.  
• M.Gaughan again voiced concern and asked the commission in as many words to proceed with 
caution. His main concern is unforeseen restrictions/consequences down the road. 
• E.Manhke voiced opinion about the density of language and suggested that it may be beneficial 
to simplify for readability and understandability.  
• S.Morgan continued to the third item, Specimen Tree definition. Language of definition is 
proposed to be aligned with the Vegetation ordinance. 
 
Motion: Proposed Amendment go to Public Hearing 20:39:00 
Motioned by: E.Mahnke 
Seconded by: J.randall 
Vote: Passes, one abstention by M.Gaughan  
Referred for public hearing on October 6th  
 
9. Commissioner Items 20:40:00 
• J.Randall called attention to the closure of Radio Bean. Asks commission to support local 
venues and cites closure of other locations recently, Nectar’s etc.  
• J.Randall called attention to the petition for two way bike lane on South Union St.   
 
10. Adopt Minutes and Accept Communications  
Action: Adopt Minutes  
Motion by: E.Mahnke 
Seconded by: E.Malone  
Vote: Passes  
Notes or Corrections: August 11th IZ meeting, Proposal 3, note to be adjusted  
 
11. Adjournment  
Action: Adjourn  
Time of Adjournment: 20:45:00 
Motion by: J.Randall  
Seconded by: E.Malone  
Vote: Passes
